note: structured entity net (22 tokens, 1 attention layer), 512 sims with tree reuse, warm-started from run2's replay buffer
_note_arch: arch=structured selects ludometer/train/net2.py: the 182-dim encoding is sliced into 6 tile-source tokens, 10 pattern-row tokens (each carrying its matching wall row), 2 wall-set tokens, 2 floor tokens, supply and globals; shared embedders per entity type, self-attention over the 22 tokens, factorised source x colour x destination policy head. Size was chosen by measurement, not by taste: 0.20 ms/position single-thread on a quiet machine (budget 0.45) and 0.66 ms with 8 workers competing, against 0.78 ms for run2's 5x768 MLP in the same 8-way test. With tree reuse turning 512 sims into ~320 evaluations per move that lands run3 at run2's self-play throughput while searching twice as deep. Re-run `python -m ludometer.train.benchmark --config configs/run3.json --games 2` before widening anything: embed=128 costs +20% and a second attention layer another +15%.
_note_pretrain: pass --pretrain runs/run2/checkpoints/replay.npz on the command line (or set "pretrain" here). The fresh structured net is fitted to run2's stored visit distributions and value targets for `pretrain_epochs` passes before any self-play, and those positions stay in the replay buffer, so iteration 1 already trains on 500k good positions instead of on noise. pretrain_lr is deliberately higher than `lr`: this phase is plain supervised learning on a large fixed dataset.
_note_lr: 60000 games x ~55 positions x 1.5 replays / 256 per batch = ~19.3k self-play steps, so lr_total_steps=20000 makes the cosine land on lr_min exactly at the end of the game budget. Peak lr is 6e-4 rather than run2's 1e-3 because the net starts pretrained: a full-size peak would undo the warm start in the first few hundred steps. lr_min 5e-5 keeps late self-play data useful without churning the weights.
_note_anchors: run1's best (+2014) is pinned so run3's curve shares run1's and run2's scale. ADD RUN2'S FINAL BEST HERE when run2 finishes: append "mcts:runs/run2/checkpoints/ckpt-XXXXXX.pt?sims=100" to eval_anchors and the same string with run2's final Elo to anchor_elos (take both from the last line of runs/run2/elo.jsonl). Until then run3 is anchored on run1 only, which is enough to keep the scale but wastes the strongest available reference.
